title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact-backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a composite canary–rollback score (verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback-success probability, LLM confidence, abstention utility) discriminates emulator-measured outages better than the best single submetric. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank, a deterministic validator, and the declared LLM (gpt-5-mini), we ran 200 held-out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded). All 200 test pairs succeeded in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0); paired-difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC-ROC primary estimand could not be computed because test labels are constant. We report this ceiling/null result with full artifact pointers and hashes, document an artifact-collection omission (the serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric CSV were not persisted), provide an authoritative stepwise recipe for deterministic reconstruction from the persisted scoring JSONs where possible, and surface concrete lessons for future discriminative NetOps evaluations.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM workflows that translate operator intent into network configuration changes are attractive for NetOps but raise assurance questions: do model-proposed changes increase outage risk? Operational safeguards commonly proposed include deterministic validators, canary deployments, and scripted rollback trials. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to evaluate whether a composite score combining verifier coverage, canary-simulation pass, rollback-success probability, model confidence, and a simple abstention-utility proxy predicts emulator-measured outage better than any single submetric. The study design, splits, estimands, and analysis plan were frozen in a machine-readable preregistration (SHA-256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). The run completed with deterministic artifacts; the principal scientific outcome is an artifact-backed null (a ceiling effect) and a set of reproducibility lessons that we report here. Research question (final): Can a preregistered composite canary–rollback score discriminate emulator-measured outage on held-out synthetic NetOps tasks better than the best single submetric? Contributions: (1) a fully artifact-backed execution record and deterministic paired analysis for N=200 held-out tasks; (2) an evidence-grounded explanation of a ceiling/null outcome and its implications for discriminative NetOps evaluation; (3) explicit artifact citations, a deterministic reconstruction recipe (limited to submetrics present in persisted artifacts), and documented omissions that prevent recomputation of the preregistered AUC-based estimand from the supplied bundle.
sections.related_work: Operational assurance for LLM-driven NetOps follows generate–verify–repair and verifier-interposition patterns and recent proposals advocating canary/rollback instrumentation and verifier orchestration (representative prior work includes intent-to-configuration and verifier-assisted pipelines [https://doi.org/10.1145/3771567], generate-verify-repair architectures for correctness-constrained generation [https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6754899], and sequential verifier-orchestration frameworks that trade verifier cost and informativeness [https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6810160]). Work on queueing and runtime-mode control for tool-augmented LLM serving shows the value of cost-aware orchestration for operational guarantees [https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6438169]. Our study is experimental and methodological: it is a preregistered paired test of a composite risk score in an emulated NetOps setting and therefore complements prior architectural and conceptual proposals by producing an artifact-traced empirical record.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 fixed: train/val/test split (train=300,val=100,test=200), primary estimand (difference in AUC-ROC: composite vs best single submetric on test), model family (declared: gpt-5-mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), adapter family (hosted_netops_gvr_v1), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), analysis pipeline (L2 logistic regression with 5-fold CV trained on train+val; paired bootstrap for CI; DeLong for AUC comparison), stopping/missingness rules, and artifact-capture requirements. The full preregistration hash is recorded in the execution manifest (SHA-256 cited above). Experiment execution. The run used a synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 (canonicalized intents, emulator-stateful topologies) and a shared-initial generation policy per task; planned_episode_count=400 (baseline+guarded), completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (execution manifest). For each episode we persisted: raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) that include deterministic validator traces and normalized configurations, and provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json). Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and the scoring JSONs include validator_trace.validation_after entries with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, and final_state. Pre-registered submetrics. The preregistration defined submetrics: (a) verifier_coverage fraction; (b) canary-sim pass rate (aggregated deterministic canonical canary simulation); (c) rollback-success probability (scripted rollback trials in emulator); (d) LLM-confidence; (e) abstention-utility proxy. Artifact capture requirement. The preregistration required persisting (i) a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV and (ii) the serialized trained-composite-model weights. Those two artifacts are not present in the supplied evidence bundle; we treat that omission transparently (see Results and Disclosure). Analysis as executed. Because all per-episode scoring JSONs and provider-call traces were persisted, the run allowed the pre-registered paired success/failure comparison between baseline and guarded condition on the held-out test. The pre-registered AUC-based comparison required a variable binary outcome across the test set; if test labels are constant the AUC comparison is uncomputable and that branch of the preregistration cannot be adjudicated from the supplied bundle.
sections.results: Authoritative, artifact-backed empirical facts. The execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; included in the evidence bundle) reports planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200. On the preregistered held-out test (N=200) the persisted per-episode scoring JSONs show baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) records n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. The paired analysis (pre-registered exact McNemar two-sided) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (seed=1729, resamples=10000) percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0]. Primary AUC estimand: uncomputable from persisted evidence. Because the held-out labels are constant (no outage positives), the preregistered AUC-based primary estimand (composite vs best single submetric) cannot be computed from the supplied evidence bundle. Artifact-collection omission. The preregistration required persisting (a) the consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV and (b) the serialized trained-composite-model weights. These two artifacts are absent from the evidence bundle. Persisted artifacts that are present and authoritative include: execution/scoring/*.json (per-episode validator traces and normalized configurations), execution/provider_calls/*.json (provider-call traces), execution/responses/*.txt (raw model outputs), execution/execution_manifest.json (run accounting), and analysis/*.csv (paired contingency and condition summary). Representative persisted-hash examples (present in the bundle): execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951. Deterministic reconciliation. The supplied deterministic_reconciliation report (artifact) confirms consistent episode accounting and provider-call audit (no cross-condition cache-key reuse observed) and is authoritative for arithmetic consistency.
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the ceiling/null outcome (artifact-grounded). The evidence indicates a ceiling effect: every held-out test task was scored VALID_CONFIGURATION by the deterministic validator in both baseline and guarded conditions. Two nonexclusive artifact-supported factors explain this: (1) the synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator/validator generated tasks solvable under the declared generation policy and model constraints (the per-episode scoring JSONs record VALID_CONFIGURATION across test episodes); (2) the deterministic validator enforces strict correctness predicates that the model-generated candidates satisfied, so the emulator labels contain no positive outage events for the test partition. Methodological implications. For discriminative evaluation of residual-risk metrics (composite canary–rollback scores) we recommend: (a) design test partitions with seeded adverse cases (fault-injection, adversarial intents, or controlled nondeterminism) to ensure a nontrivial positive label rate; (b) persist trained-model artifacts and consolidated submetric summaries as part of routine artifact hygiene so the full preregistered discriminative analysis is reproducible; (c) balance deterministic validators (which improve reproducibility) with calibrated emulator nondeterminism that exercises canary/rollback discriminators. Reproducibility & reconstruction. The evidence bundle allows deterministic reconstruction of some quantities; see Reproduction Recipe below. Missing persisted artifacts (trained weights and consolidated submetric CSV) prevent recomputing the preregistered AUC comparison from the supplied bundle without creating new derived artifacts. We do not fabricate such derived artifacts here; instead we provide the deterministic reconstruction recipe that an independent party could execute against the persisted scoring JSONs to reproduce the composite training steps if they persist or regenerate the consolidated submetric CSV and trained weights.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment testing a composite canary–rollback risk score on a synthetic NetOps task bank with deterministic validation. The empirical outcome on the preregistered held-out test was a ceiling/null: both baseline and guarded succeeded on all 200 pairs (paired difference 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). The preregistered AUC-ROC primary estimand could not be evaluated because test labels are constant; additionally, two preregistered artifacts required for deterministic recomputation of the composite-vs-submetric AUC comparison (the serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric CSV) were not persisted. The principal contribution is methodological and practical: an artifact-traced record of a null ceiling effect plus explicit, evidence-grounded recommendations for future discriminative NetOps evaluations (seeded failure cases, artifact hygiene, and calibrated emulator nondeterminism). We release the preserved execution and scoring artifacts (paths and SHA-256s cited below) so the community can reproduce the documented facts and use the preserved traces to design richer test partitions that avoid the ceiling effect observed here. Reproduction Recipe (deterministic steps using persisted artifacts). The following deterministic reconstruction steps use only artifacts present in the evidence bundle. Where a required submetric field is not present in the persisted JSONs we mark that step as "requires missing artifact" and treat it transparently: 1) Obtain persisted per-episode scoring JSONs: execution/scoring/*.json (representative example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63...4478). 2) Build per-episode labels: extract validator_trace.validation_after.valid (boolean) to form the binary outcome label (0/1). This yields the outcome vector used in the paired contingency. 3) Compute verifier_coverage (available from persisted validator fields): verifier_coverage := validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count / validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count. These two numeric fields are present in the scoring JSONs. 4) Canary-sim pass / rollback-success / LLM-confidence / abstention-utility: the preregistered submetrics were to be recorded in the consolidated per-episode submetric CSV, but the bundle does NOT contain that consolidated CSV nor a serialized per-episode submetric summary. If these submetrics were recorded in execution/provider_calls/*.json they can be deterministically extracted; check provider-call entries for explicit canary_sim_result, rollback_trial_result, model_confidence, or abstain_decision entries. If those fields are absent, reconstructing these submetrics requires (a) re-running deterministic canary/rollback simulation code that is not persisted in the evidence bundle, or (b) using missing persisted artifacts (the consolidated CSV). Because those artifacts are absent we mark composite training as uncomputable from the supplied bundle without deriving new artifacts. 5) If step 4 provides the full submetric table (it may not), then: assemble the per-episode feature matrix (verifier_coverage, canary_pass, rollback_prob, model_confidence, abstention_utility), use the preregistered L2 logistic regression with 5-fold CV on train+val to obtain weights (record CV folds deterministically by the preregistered hash-based split), freeze weights, apply to test to compute continuous composite score, and compute AUC-ROC and AUPRC with DeLong and paired bootstrap (seed=1729, resamples=10000) as preregistered. Practical reproduction caveat: the supplied bundle does not include the consolidated per-episode submetric CSV nor the serialized trained-composite-model weights; therefore steps 4–5 cannot be completed using only the supplied artifacts unless the missing submetrics can be deterministically extracted from provider_call traces (search execution/provider_calls/*.json for canary/rollback/model-confidence entries). If such fields are absent, the missing persisted artifacts prevent recomputation of the preregistered AUC comparison. Recommended immediate fixes for future runs (artifact hygiene): always persist (i) consolidated per-episode submetric CSV, (ii) trained-model weights file, (iii) explicit mapping document (field names used for each preregistered submetric), and (iv) a short deterministic retrain script path with hash so independent third parties can recompute composite weights from persisted primitives. These files were required by the preregistration but are missing from the bundle (documented omission). Representative persisted artifact pointers and hashes (authoritative): execution/execution_manifest.json (manifested in the evidence bundle), execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c, analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951. Full execution and analysis manifests are in the supplied evidence bundle and should be consulted for deterministic reproduction of the reported accounting facts (paths and full hash manifest are included).

disclosure_statement: Autonomy, pre-lock human role, and immutable initial master prompt. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment-design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared LLM and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1; the preregistration JSON SHA-256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee (recorded in the execution manifest). Evidence retention and omission. The evidence bundle contains per-episode raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json — representative example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv) with recorded SHA-256 hashes (representative hashes cited in the manuscript). The preregistered artifacts that were NOT persisted into the evidence bundle are (a) the serialized trained-composite-model weights file and (b) a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV. Because those two artifacts were not persisted, the preregistered AUC-ROC composite-vs-best-submetric discriminative comparison cannot be recomputed from the supplied bundle without deterministic reconstruction from the raw scoring JSONs and retraining (a derived computation that would create new artifacts). Safety and operational scope. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). All retained artifacts are hashed and listed in the execution manifest; representative hashes are cited above and in the manuscript.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact-collection omission).
